clue.text: Heading off to give credit for writer

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so removing the heading takes away its opening letter

parts.note: to ascribe something to someone is to give them credit for it

explanation.surface: Instructions to remove a heading before crediting the author of a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' strips the first letter, A, from ASCRIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is a person who writes, especially one copying documents by hand.

clue.text: Cabinetmaker inside fascinates her at once

indicators.note: the answer sits within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A furniture craftsman instantly charming a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton was an eighteenth-century English furniture designer.

clue.text: Easily irritated principal's dropped out of practice

indicators.note: the principal letter is the first one, and it is removed

parts.note: crusty means short-tempered and irritable

explanation.surface: A grumpy head teacher who has left a practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Rusty describes skills that have deteriorated through lack of use.

clue.text: Club about to lose support? Just the opposite

indicators.note: losing takes one piece away from another
reverses the roles, so the support loses the about rather than the other way round

parts.note: a brassiere is a supporting undergarment
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A golf club in danger of losing its backing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'about to lose support' suggests the club is losing its backing; 'Just the opposite' tells you to swap the roles, so the undergarment is what loses the little word for about. A brassie is an old wooden golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassie is an old name for a number two wood in golf.

clue.text: Choose not to take part in work with aggressive seller

parts.note: OP is the standard abbreviation for opus, a musical work
a tout pushes goods or tickets on passers-by

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to join in with a pushy salesman's job.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt out is the idiom for declining to participate in a scheme.

clue.text: Gnome in lead crossing river beyond

indicators.note: the outer piece stretches across the others, holding them inside

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
over can mean beyond, as in over the hill

explanation.surface: A garden gnome made of lead straddling a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnome' looks like the garden ornament; here it means a maxim.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome is a short pithy saying, so it is a synonym of a maxim or adage.

clue.text: Her co-star upset big band

indicators.note: knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: An actress's fellow star upsetting a large musical group.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of musicians playing together.

clue.text: Pinch this short girl

indicators.note: cut short, so the word this loses its last letter

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Squeezing a small girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinch is slang for steal, which is what thieves do.

clue.text: Judge, we recalled, pointed instrument

indicators.note: called back, so the little word we is turned to run backwards

parts.note: sharp means having a point

explanation.surface: A judge remembering a sharp musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A jew's harp is a small twanging instrument held between the teeth.

clue.text: Snap decision at end of race?

definitions.text: Snap decision at end of race?

parts.words: Snap decision at end of race?
parts.note: a snap is a photograph, and a close race is decided by a picture at the line

explanation.surface: A hasty choice made when a race finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo finish is a race result so close it is settled by a photograph of the line.

clue.text: Gold cross initially concealed in plant

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of the word cross

parts.note: hid means concealed

explanation.surface: Treasure and a cross buried in a flowerbed.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is a flowering plant with showy, often exotic blooms.

clue.text: Cautious fighting against unknown quantity

parts.note: war is armed fighting
in algebra x and y stand for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: Someone hesitant about going into battle against an unpredictable foe.
explanation.definitionFit: Wary is a synonym for careful and watchful of danger.

clue.text: A sailor can't take this on board

definitions.text: A sailor can't take this on board

parts.words: A sailor can't take this on board
parts.note: on board seems to mean understand, but the time off in question can only be spent ashore, off the ship

explanation.surface: A seaman who just cannot grasp some idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Shore leave is a sailor's permitted time off spent on land rather than aboard ship.

clue.text: Both comrades injured, so out of action

explanation.surface: Two soldiers wounded and so unable to fight on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' rearranges the twelve letters of BOTH COMRADES.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase hors de combat, used in English, means disabled and unable to fight.

clue.text: Religious ceremony in US city, unfinished

indicators.note: not completed, so the last letter is left off

parts.note: Sacramento is the capital of California

explanation.surface: A church service held in an American city.

explanation.definitionFit: A sacrament is a Christian rite such as baptism or communion.

clue.text: Merry at last in idyllic island

indicators.note: tipsy, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: Finally happy on a paradise island.

clue.text: Pie (any sort) and chips cooked

explanation.surface: Ordering a pie of whatever kind with chips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges ANY SORT plus CHIPS; 'and' only joins. A Cornish pasty is a British folded pastry of meat and vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cornish pasty is a traditional baked pastry pie from Cornwall.

clue.text: Article misrepresented performance

indicators.note: presented wrongly, so the letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece giving a false account of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a solo or small-group musical performance.

clue.text: Abbreviated answer printed in tough political publication

indicators.note: written inside, so one piece goes within the other

indicators.note: shortened, so the word answer is cut down to its usual short form, keeping only its first three letters

explanation.surface: A brief reply appearing in a hard-hitting political paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Hansard is the official printed record of UK parliamentary debates.
explanation.definitionFit: Hansard is the verbatim published report of proceedings in the British Parliament.

clue.text: A vet disturbed over service in bar

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is an inn or public house serving drinks.

clue.text: Book country hotel

parts.note: Jamaica is a Caribbean country

explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb meaning reserve; it is the noun, a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamaica Inn is a 1936 novel by Daphne du Maurier, so it is a named book.

clue.text: Lover's knot, say

clue.text: Little child I found in farm building

parts.note: a barn is a farm storage building

explanation.surface: A small child discovered in a barn.

clue.text: Failing to change sides

to desert one's country or party for the other

explanation.definitionFit: Defect means both an imperfection and abandoning one's allegiance.

clue.text: Flower husband presented to poorly Cynthia

indicators.note: unwell, so the name's letters are put out of order

clue.text: Annoy the Parisian after final

indicators.note: places the French word behind the preceding piece

parts.note: nett, a spelling of net, means final, as in a figure after all deductions
le is French for the

explanation.definitionFit: To nettle someone is to irritate them, like a nettle's sting.

clue.text: A college teacher is one killed while hunting

parts.note: a don is a university or college lecturer

explanation.surface: An academic who died on a hunt.
